answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays with path length rather than accumulating through arbitrary chains. If a sybil cluster has low conductance—a small boundary relative to its volume—few walks enter or leave it; under a fixed honest seed distribution and capped per-node influence, its voting weight is bounded by that boundary flow. Min-cut bounds constrain transitive amplification, whether nodes are labeled atlas, orchard, or basalt.
